label: Meditation III idea-of-the-infinite argument and the cogito: premise map and missing GOD_4 bridge
summary: Analyst reconstruction, attribution deferred (navigation only: Descartes, Meditation III and the Second Replies axioms; no source records). Not formalized in this PR for scope (the Cartesian adequacy comparison of the same branch came first, about 30 files); this records the premise map for the follow-up. (1) Faithful core of the idea-of-the-infinite argument over the grades frame F plus the cogito binders Occurs and Bears (definition 8181eef7, ThinkingRootFork.Thinks), with a designated meditator me : B and a respect inf for 'infinite substance': P1 (new) some occurring episode e borne by me represents inf, i.e. Occurs e ∧ Bears me e ∧ Represents e inf; P2 (new) the objective reality of every occurring idea has a cause: Occurs e → Represents e r → ∃ c, ObjCause c e r; P3 (new) objective adequacy: ObjCause c e r → F.InAct c r (formally or eminently, the open mode of IN_ACT_4); P4 (new) finitude of the meditator: ¬ F.InAct me inf. Conclusion: ∃ c, c ≠ me ∧ F.InAct c inf; with the existing ActualityOnlyInsofarAsBeing (7067553d) also F.InAct c F.esse. New primitives needed: Represents : Episode → R → Prop (objective reality, the idea presents r) and ObjCause : B → Episode → R → Prop (cause of an idea's objective r-reality). Reused nodes: the containment hinge only through P3 (see (2)), the cogito binders, 7067553d. (2) Rejected reading: P3 as an instance of the formal containment clause (ContainmentInTotalCause of this branch). Encoding objective reality as a respect obj r with ObjIn e r := InAct e (obj r), formal containment gives only that the cause of e's representing r is in act in obj r (it has the representing feature), not r itself. The objective version is therefore a separate premise (navigation: the Second Replies list it as a separate axiom); a finite model with the meditator causing its own representing feature, satisfying formal containment and violating P3, would certify the separation. This is the precise locus of the standard objection that an idea of the infinite needs only a cause able to represent infinity (target P3; mechanism: equivocation between containing r and containing a representation of r; independent justification: the formal clause, as encoded, does not entail P3). (3) Rejected reading: finitude as 'every thinker lacks inf'. With P1-P3 it makes the infinite cause a non-thinker, which conflicts with the intellect attributes the route later needs (supremely intelligent) and is stronger than the first-person premise; P4 is about the meditator only. (4) Exact missing bridge to an existing God-existence node: GOD_4 existence (8626f8a5) needs a naming bridge from 'in act in inf' to GOD_4, either directly (whatever is in act, formally or eminently, in the perfection of infinite substance is GOD_4) or via maximality (whatever is in act in inf is maximal in being, IsMaximumIn F.InAct F.MoreIn F.esse) followed by the existing maxime-ens naming (957a71fe, GOD_2) and the GOD_2-to-GOD_4 bridges of the existing routes. Blocker: no corpus statement relates a perfection respect 'infinite' to INFINITE_1 (b0132989 runs from GOD_4 to INFINITE_1, the opposite direction) or to maximality in being; such a bridge is an open analyst premise to be added with its own definition of the inf respect. (5) The cogito (#1797 route): the existing premises are existential and subjectless at their base: ThoughtOccurs (e81971f1, ∃ e, Occurs e) and the bearer principle (30e6e01c) give Thinks x for some x. The first-person 'I think' (∃ e, Occurs e ∧ Bears me e) would strengthen ThoughtOccurs (immediate, not yet a registered result) and directly gives an existential bearer without the bearer principle; it thus carries that principle's content for this case (the existing control 6cffb105 has a thought with no bearer). The cogito supplies Thinks, not world-indexed existence (EveryBearerExistsAt, c821487b, is a separate bridge: Occurs is not world-indexed), not concreteness, not finitude, not identity of the bearer with the meditator of P1. In the Meditation III argument it supplies only P1's 'Bears me e' part, and only in the first-person version. (6) Clear-and-distinct perception is not a premise of any step above, so the Cartesian-circle objection has no target on this route. (7) Not here: the Meditation V ontological argument belongs to the existence-as-a-predicate cluster (branch agent/existence-predicate-cluster) and is left as a pointer for that follow-up.
blocker: Formalize P1-P4 with the Represents and ObjCause primitives and their definitions, the objective/formal separation model, and the first-person cogito strength order over ThoughtOccurs; then add the open naming bridge from the inf respect to GOD_4 (or to maximality in being) with a definition of that respect. No existing statement supplies that bridge.
